High Court Of Judicature Madhya Pradesh,
 Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Kanhaiya Lal Vs. State of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Shri D.K. Melani, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri G.S. Thakur, learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/ State.

This criminal revision has been filed by the applicant under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C. against the judgment dated 18.02.2000 passed by the Seventh Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur in Criminal Appeal No. 122/2000 arising out of the judgment dated 27.10.1999 passed by the JMFC and Special Magistrate, Jabalpur in Criminal Complaint Case No. 1338/1996 whereby the applicant has been convicted under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1) (a)(i) of the Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months and a fine of Rs.1,000/-; in default of payment of fine, he has been further sentenced to undergo two months' R.I.
2.

entities.text: Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In brief the facts of the case are that on 09.05.1994, Food Inspector visited the milk dairy of the applicant Kanhaiya Lal situated at Dwarika Nagar, Lalmati, Jabalpur.

After disclosing his identity,
he purchased 750 ml of milk and as per the due procedure the same was sent for examination to the Public Analyst for his report, wherein the milk was found to be adulterated.

Subsequently, a private complaint was filed by the Food Inspector before the JMFC and the JMFC, after recording the evidence recording conviction against the applicant as mentioned above and being aggrieved of the same, criminal appeal was preferred by the applicant before the lower appellate Court, which was also dismissed.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that in the present case, he has been convicted of an offence punishable under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred to as Kanhaiya Lal vs The State Of M.P. on 6 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133520962/
1 'Act'), which provides a detailed procedure to be followed to prosecute a person and certain mandatory provisions of the aforesaid Act has not been followed by the learned Judge of the Trial Court, which have been over-looked by the learned appellate Court as well.
4.

entities.text: Kanhaiya Lal vs The State Of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted in the petition that the samples were taken on 9.5.1994.

The report of the Public Analyst was received on 20.06.1994 and the matter was sent to the Central Government for obtaining consent to file complaint and the consent was provided on 23.09.1996, which is inordinate delay in prosecuting the applicant.
No explanation has been provided for such an inordinate delay.
On this ground, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the complaint itself should be thrown out of the Court.

It is further submitted that the documents filed along with the complaint have not been proved as only photocopies have been filed by the complainant, which have been exhibited without formal proof and it is further submitted that the applicant was not issued requisite notice as provided under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, which has led to serious prejudice to him.

So far as the right to get the sample examination is concerned, it is further submitted that after the applicant submitted the application on 30.01.1999 to get the sample examined through the Central Food Laboratory, he also deposited requisite fees for the same and the orders in this behalf were passed by the learned J.M.F.C. on 17.03.1999 to produce the samples to be sent for examination by Central Food Laboratory but samples were not brought to the Court on 22.03.1999, 24.03.1999, 5.4.1999 and the samples were produced only on 12.04.1999

whereas under Section 13(2-A) it is provided that when an application is made to the Court under sub-section (2), the Court shall require the Local (Health)
Authority to forward the part or parts of the sample kept by the said Authority and upon such requisition being made, the said Authority shall forward the part or parts of the sample to the Court within a period of five days from the date of receipt of such requisition.
Thus, it is submitted that non-compliance of Section 13(2-A) of the Act has vitiated the entire trial and on this ground also, the impugned orders are liable to be set aside.

It is further submitted that the trial Court has framed charges against the applicant under Section 2(a)(d) of the Act and as such no specific charges have been framed against him which has led to the prejudice against him as he could not lead the evidence to counter charges under which ultimately he was convicted.

It is further stated that regarding Ex. P/12 which is the report, the applicant has not been put specific questions in his accused statement and under these circumstances, his conviction is bad in law.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

From the record, this Court finds that the samples from the applicant's shop were taken on 9.5.1994 and one out of three samples of the same was sent to local Food Authority on 9.5.1994 itself and other two samples were sealed properly and were sent to the Chief Medical and Health Officer,
Jabalpur.
A report from the State Food Laboratory was received on 20.06.1994.

The record also reveals that although various photocopies of the aforesaid documents were filed by the prosecution but in the deposition of the complainant it is clearly mentioned that the same have been compared with the originals and the originals have been returned back to the concerned persons and as such the veracity of those documents which have already been exhibited cannot be doubted.

Kanhaiya Lal vs The State Of M.P. on 6 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133520962/
2 7.

entities.text: Kanhaiya Lal vs The State Of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the milk was found to be adulterated and although sanction to prosecute was given on 23.09.1996 i.e. after about 2 years but in the considered opinion of this Court, mere delay in granting sanction cannot be a ground to challenge the entire proceedings especially when under Section 470 of the Code of Criminal procedure, it is specifically provided that the time taken by the Government to grant sanction to prosecute has to be excluded while counting the period of limitation.
In view of the same, the contention raised by the learned counsel for the applicant that there was inordinate delay, cannot be accepted.

8. This Court also finds that although the applicant has raised the objection regarding non-compliance of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 in respect of non-receipt of the notice from the Food Inspector regarding the samples which he may examine from Central Food Laboratory but it is also apparent that the applicant has exercised his right to get the samples examined from Central Food Laboratory on 15.03.1999 and the aforesaid application was filed way beyond the period of limitation as is provided under Section 13(2) of the Act, but still the aforesaid application was allowed and subsequently, report Ex.P/14. from Central Food Laboratory was received in which also milk was found to be adulterated.

entities.text: Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: So far as the objection raised by the counsel for the applicant that while requisitioning the samples, the provision of Section 13(2-A) have not been followed, the same appears to be correct, however, due to such non-compliance, what prejudice is caused to the applicant, has not been stated.
On the other hand, a bare perusal of Section 13(2-A) of the Act reveals that its language directory only and has been enacted with a view to expedite proceedings and nothing more.
Thus, it is held that non- compliance of s.13(2-A) would not render the entire trial vitiated as the same is not mandatory in nature.
9. So far as the framing of charges is concerned, it is also apparent from the order-sheet dated 19.02.1997 that appropriate charges were framed against the petitioner.

From the questionnaire under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. it is apparent that all the relevant questions have been put to the applicant hence the contention that no specific question was put to the applicant regarding the report P/12 in his statement under s. 313 is also incorrect as the same has indeed been put to him to which he has replied in negative.

10. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court is of the considered opinion that no case for interference is made out in this revision as all the mandatory provisions of the Food Adulteration Act have been complied with by the prosecution.

However, so far as the sentence part is concerned, although the applicant has been sentenced with the minimum sentence of 6 months under s.16 of the Act but still, the same requires some consideration and in this regard Proviso(i) to the first proviso to s.16 can be invoked which provides that for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment, a sentence of imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months may be imposed.
This court finds that when the offence took place on 09.05.1994 i.e. around 23 years ago, the age of the applicant was 58 years and as such by now he must have been somewhere around 82 years of age.
The order sheet dated 04.02.2008 also reveals that looking to the physical condition of the applicant that he was unable to walk, this court had granted permanent exemption from appearance.

In such circumstances, when in the year 2008 itself the applicant was unable to walk due to old age and Kanhaiya Lal vs The State Of M.P. on 6 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133520962/
3 various diseases, it can be presumed that his condition must have been deteriorated from bad to worse.

entities.text: Kanhaiya Lal vs The State Of M.P. on 6 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, it would not be proper to sentence him for a period of six months and instead, he is sentenced to three months R.I. only.
The revision is accordingly allowed to the aforesaid extent.
C.C. As per rules.
(Subodh Abhyankar) Judge Vikram Date: 2018.02.07 16:08:03 +05'30'
